'''''Begonia rex''''', the '''king begonia''', '''fancy-leaf begonia,''' or '''painted-leaf begonia''' is a species of flowering plant in the family [[Begoniaceae]]. It is a [[rhizomatous]] begonia first brought to England from [[Assam]], and documented in 1857.<ref name="ABS">{{cite web |last1=Tsamtsis |first1=Paul |title=''Begonia rex'' Putzeys |url=https://www.begonias.org/begonia-rex-putzeys/ |website=begonias.org |publisher=American Begonia Society |access-date=16 December 2025 |ref=ABS }}</ref>

It is native to the [[East Himalayas]], found from southern Bhutan to northern Myanmar, and has been introduced to Bangladesh, Cuba, the Dominican Republic, and Haiti.<ref name="105573-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:105573-1 |title=''Begonia rex'' Putz. |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=17 December 2025 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=''Begonia rex'' king begonia |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/101666/i-Begonia-rex-i-(R)/Details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=6 July 2021 |quote=Other common names; … fan plant, painted-leaf begonia }}</ref>

These plants are noted for their dark leaves with prominent silvery grey bands, and are usually grown for their foliage, not flowers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=ABS |date=7 June 2021 |title=Join {{!}} American Begonia Society |url=https://www.begonias.org/membership/join/ |access-date=24 January 2026 |website=www.begonias.org |language=en-US }}</ref> When this species was introduced into cultivation, it became popular as a houseplant. Hybrids began to appear with varying leaf patterns as Rex begonias hybridize quite freely.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shannon |first=Laughlin |date=23 February 2022 |title=Rex Begonia {{!}} Home and Garden Education Center |url=https://homegarden.cahnr.uconn.edu/factsheets/rex-begonia/ |access-date=28 September 2024 |website=[[University of Connecticut]] |language=en-US }}</ref>

==Rex Cultorum==

''Begonia rex'' Putz. was thought to be good [[type species]] until [[molecular taxonomy]] revealed that it is likely only one member of a large [[species complex]] of closely related begonias with similar appearances. The complex and its hybrid progeny are collectively referred to as Begonia Rex Cultorum.<ref name="Cultorum">{{cite web |title=Rex Cultorum |url=https://www.begonias.org/rex-cultorum/ |website=begonias.org |publisher=American Begonia Society |access-date=16 December 2025 |ref=Cultorum }}</ref>

''Begonia rex'' is in the parentage of over 500 cultivars in the Begonia Rex Cultorum [[Cultivar group|Group]] of [[houseplants]].<ref name = "CubeyWesley" >{{cite journal |last1=Cubey |first1=Janet |last2=Wesley |first2=Wendy |date=December 2006 |title=Begonia Rex Cultorum Group |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/PDFs/Plant-trials-and-awards/Plant-bulletins/begonia-rex.pdf |journal=RHS Plant Trials and Awards |volume=Bulletin Number 16 |pages=1–16 |access-date=6 July 2021 }}</ref>

Other parents in the multitude of crosses made during the creation of the Group include ''[[Begonia annulata]]'', ''[[Begonia cathayana|B.{{nbsp}}cathayana]]'', ''[[Begonia decora|B.{{nbsp}}decora]]'', ''[[Begonia diadema|B.{{nbsp}}diadema]]'', ''[[Begonia dregei|B.{{nbsp}}dregei]]'', ''[[Begonia grandis|B.{{nbsp}}grandis]]'', ''[[Begonia hatacoa|B.{{nbsp}}hatacoa]]'', ''[[Begonia palmata|B.{{nbsp}}palmata]]'', and ''[[Begonia xanthina|B.{{nbsp}}xanthina]]''.<ref name = "CubeyWesley" />

Other cultivars that have also received [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]] include: 'Carolina Moon', 'China Curl', 'Curly Fireflush', 'David Blais', 'Dewdrop', 'Emerald Beauty', 'Green Gold', 'Helen Lewis', 'Hilo Holiday', 'Ironstone', 'Martin Johnson', 'Mikado', 'Orient', 'Pink Champagne', 'Princess of Hanover', 'Red Robin', 'Regal Minuet', 'Rocheart', 'Roi de Roses', 'Sal's Comet', 'Sea Serpent', 'Silver Cloud', and 'Silver King'.<ref>{{cite web |title=AGM Plants Dec 2020 © RHS – ORNAMENTAL |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/pdfs/agm-lists/agm-ornamentals.pdf |date=December 2020 |website=rhs.org.uk |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=6 July 2021 }}</ref>

== Light ==
Rex begonias do well in bright, indirect light. Foliage of these plants could burn when plants are exposed to excessive direct sunlight. The ideal [[Luminous intensity|light intensity]] for most Rex begonia varieties is 1,500 to 2,200 foot-candles.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ginori |first=Julian |last2=Huo |first2=Heqiang |last3=Norman |first3=Dave |date=12 December 2022 |title=Beginner's Guide to Begonias: Begonia rex-cultorum |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.32473/edis-ep632-2022 |journal=EDIS |volume=2022 |issue=6 |doi=10.32473/edis-ep632-2022 |issn=2576-0009 |doi-access=free }}</ref>
